extracted.intended_audience: aspiring writers, literary critics, and students of literature
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical criteria for assessing or producing refined literary prose (specifically discussion of Euphuism and related stylistic practice): what counts as good style, where mannerism begins, and how matter and expression should relate. Useful for writers, critics, and students studying prose aesthetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care for style and patience of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: “What care for style! what patience of execution! what research for the significant tones of ancient idiom—sonantia verba et antiqua! What stately and regular word-building—gravis et decora constructio!”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend closely to wording, cadence, and the ‘tone’ of idiom; invest time and research in choosing stately, regular constructions. Style should be deliberately cultivated, with attention to how each phrase contributes to overall effect and dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore the natural, direct relation between thought and expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should “re-establish the natural and direct relationship between thought and expression, between the sensation and the term, and restore to words their primitive power.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a close, immediate linkage of perception and wording so that language conveys sensation directly. Avoid stale or routine phrasing that separates idea from apt expression; revive original, forceful senses of words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat words as the primary instrument — know their exact value and power
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer must have “a fine instinctive sentiment of the exact value and power of words... Words... were to be the apparatus of a war for himself.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select words for their resonances and capacities to move readers; use diction strategically to make visible what the writer perceives. Words should be handled as tools of persuasion and revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceal the art (ars est celare artem)
rubrics_metrics.description: “’Tis art’s function to conceal itself: ars est celare artem.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polish and refinement should not call attention to themselves; the labour behind fine writing ought to be invisible in the final effect. Elegance should feel natural rather than showy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meticulous revision ('labour of the file') enriches work
rubrics_metrics.description: The ‘labour of the file’ is described as a labour which, like the goldsmith’s, “enriching the work by far more than the weight of precious metal it removed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value careful editing and minute reworking of phrasing: revision is not mere subtraction but an act of enrichment. Persistent refinement often yields disproportionate improvement in the finished piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive mannerism, foppery, and neologisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Euphuism “might lapse into its characteristic fopperies or mannerisms, into the ‘defects of its qualities’... its neologies were the ground of one of the favourite charges against it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of mannered tricks, affected prettiness, and gratuitous coinages. While some stylistic quirks may be pardonable in a highly cultivated age, they risk undermining sincerity and clarity when overused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style must be grounded in genuine matter and personal intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: A saving principle is “this uncompromising demand for a matter, in all art, derived immediately from lively personal intuition, which saved his euphuism... from lapsing into mere artifice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that stylistic refinement serves real intellectual or emotional substance. Without authentic matter or conviction, ornament becomes hollow; style should arise from and serve genuine intuition or insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be genuinely interested — personal interest precedes interest in others
rubrics_metrics.description: “To know when one’s self is interested, is the first condition of interesting other people.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers must cultivate and recognize their own lively interest in a subject to engage readers. Sincerity of attention and appetite for the material is foundational to persuasive and compelling writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance classical authority with vernacular freshness
rubrics_metrics.description: The literary programme is described as “partly conservative or reactionary... partly popular and revolutionary, asserting... the rights of the proletariate of speech,” reviving ancient idiom while drawing on colloquial gems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine reverence for classical forms and tones with responsiveness to the living vernacular. Reviving ancient expressions and figurative power is valuable, but so is harvesting fresh, vivid turns of speech from common usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use technical devices (e.g., refrain) judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: In Euphuism “in the composition of verse, its fancy for the refrain... It was a snatch from a popular chorus... that Flavian had chosen for the refrain of a poem he was then pondering—the Pervigilium Veneris.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ devices like refrain and popular motifs where they enhance effect, but avoid dependence on them as mere mannerisms. Such devices can give music and familiarity to verse if integrated with substance rather than used as ornament alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept historical and aesthetic differences; avoid forced imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A true literary tact “would accept that difference in forming the primary conception of the literary function at a later time... Perhaps the utmost one could get by conscious effort... would be novitas, artificial artlessness, naïveté.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that direct imitation of an earlier age’s freshness is limited; understand historical context and adjust expectations. Strive for authenticity rather than contrived revival; novelty produced by strain will often betray artifice.
